v1.feedback: The radial pop-wave expanding outward with a temporary ink→raspberry color shift is a genuine, well-targeted interpretation of 'raspberry-pop' — the idea clearly drove the shader, not just a palette swap. The calyx cup form reads in under 2s, and the restrained ink base with transient raspberry accent is tasteful. To refine: the pop ring could be sharper (tighten the smoothstep band from 3.0 to ~1.5 so the color front is a crisp expanding ring rather than a soft wash), the upward displacement during pop (1.8 units) is modest enough that it barely registers at default camera distance — consider scaling it to 3.0+ or adding a brief z-scatter so the 'seeds popping' read more dramatically, and the 12-second pop cycle feels slightly sluggish on repeat — stagger a second smaller pop at a different radius or vary the interval to keep the surprise alive across loops.

v2.feedback: The raspberry-pop concept lands well — the staggered ring-burst with berry-pink particles erupting from the calyx cup is a legible surprise moment, and the palette swerve (ink → raspberry) is restrained and tasteful. The flat-grid → cupped-flower morph gives recognizable botanical form within 2s, satisfying the calyx lineage. Two things to tighten: the pop waves dissipate quickly and the piece spends most of its time as a quiet ink-toned cup with no color — consider letting a faint residual blush linger on recently-popped particles (e.g. decay vPopIntensity over 5s instead of 3s) so the raspberry identity persists between bursts. Also the camera sits high and distant; pulling camera.position.z to ~14 and lowering the FOV to 32 would fill more frame with the cup form, avoiding the small-subject-in-vast-canvas trap.
